summary: Uneven per-key token buckets causing intermittent 429s across multiplexed API keys
description: Issue summary: Customer reports sporadic 429 responses even though aggregate request rate is within their committed throughput. Impact: Intermittent failures for two internal services (search indexing and live-catalog rerank) causing ~2–5% request failure spikes during mid-day. Environment: Dedicated pool in us-east, tenant BrightSearch (dedicated contract). Steps to reproduce: 1) Use three API keys belonging to the same org and run multiplexed short-text generation (50–100 req/min per key) against /v1/generate with streaming disabled. 2) Observe 429s on one of the keys after several minutes even though overall token rate < reserved capacity. 3) Re-running with only a single key removes 429s. Logs/observations: Customer provided screenshots showing 429 responses tagged with quota_id: "org-7689-global" and sub_bucket: "key-03". They also shared a pcap showing consistent connection success, only rejected by server with 429 body referencing "per-key bucket exhausted".
comments: 2026-03-10 Miguel Rivera: Acknowledged ticket. Asking for request IDs and example timestamps to correlate with gateway logs. Recommended temporary mitigation: rotate keys and isolate traffic to a single key while we investigate.

2026-03-10 Aisha Khan (customer): Provided three sample request_ids: rQe-20260310-01, rQe-20260310-02, rQe-20260310-03 and timestamps (2026-03-10T14:22:05Z - 14:28:34Z). Confirmed failures only on key-03.

2026-03-11 SRE (Liam O'Connor): Pulling api-gateway and quota-manager logs for org-7689 during window. Noted per-key token-bucket refill misalignment after a recent rolling deploy of quota-manager (PR #2041). Recommending throttle config review and possible backfill fix.
2026-03-11 Miguel Rivera: Asked customer to run a small paced load test (10 req/min per key) and report whether 429s still occur. Also asked for their console quota config screenshot.

2026-03-11 Aisha Khan (customer): Confirmed 429s persist at low rate on key-03. Shared console screenshot showing global throughput 1200 tpm reserved, and per-key override was not set. All three keys appear under same project with default per-key assignment.

2026-03-12 SRE (Priya Patel): Confirmed a bug in per-key bucket assignment logic when multiple API keys share the same org bucket and multiplexed connections are used. Created INT-4492 for the code fix on quota-manager (token-bucket alignment and drift correction).
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: per-key bucket configured incorrectly during rolling deploy leading to mismatched refill intervals for key shards.

Gateway evidence: 429 responses have header X-RateLimit-Reason: per_key_exhausted and quota_id field matches org bucket. Token consumption counts show key-03 counters incrementing faster relative to refill ticks.

SRE reproduction: Local replay with three keys reproduced 429 on key-03 when gateway version v2.9.1 was fronting quota-manager v1.7.0; alignment fixed when we forced single-version mapping (temporary workaround).

Telemetry note: observed small clock skew between quota-manager instances (up to 150ms) exacerbated by staggered refill windows. Combined with burst allowance, this caused one shard to run dry while others had tokens.
Risk assessment: Medium — affects only multiplexed multi-key setups in dedicated pools after last quota-manager deploy. No data loss, but service degradation for some keys.
Related PRs/threads: github.com/redwood/quota-manager PR #2041 (deploy) and internal slack thread #support-rate-limits archived link: slack://channel/support-rate-limits/2026-03-11
resolution: Mitigation applied: SRE rolled back quota-manager to v1.6.9 for the affected pool which restored aligned refill behavior and eliminated 429s for BrightSearch. For a durable fix, INT-4492 created to implement refill tick consensus and drift-correction logic; target hotfix release v1.7.1. Customer actions recommended: (1) split high-throughput workloads across distinct project-level buckets when using many concurrent keys, (2) enable per-key rate overrides in Console for critical keys, (3) monitor the new per-key metrics panel in Console once hotfix is deployed. Follow-up: schedule post-deploy verification with customer (assigned to Miguel) and update customer on INT-4492 progress.
